newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up vs dlr in spot, forward markets.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up vs dlr in spot, forward markets.

text.p: The Indian rupee gained against the dollar in both the forward and spot markets in mid-morning Monday trade as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept off the market, dealers said.
They said the rupee moved up to 35.83/84 from the weekend close of 35.840-845 as the principal buyer of dollars in recent months, the RBI, kept away from the market.
RBI dollar purchases pushed the rupee down from last Monday's opening of 35.75 per dollar to 35.89 on Wednesday before it rallied to current levels.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.827/837 rupees.
"So far they (RBI) haven't come to the market," said a dealer at a private bank. "Without RBI buying, the rupee looks to be headed only one way at the moment....up."
Dealers said the rupee gained on Monday on forward and spot dollar sales by corporates.
In the forward market, November-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 88/92 paise against the weekend close of 92/94.
"Premiums came down as call money has eased," said a dealer.
Call money was traded at 8.0-8.25 percent in mid-morning on Monday against against weekend close of 8.5-8.75.
"But I do not think there will be much change in forward premiums from current levels," the dealer said.
